_note: Mock agents for the demo user. Each intent runs ONE engine function with the request's inputs and fills {paths} from the engine result. `variants` pick a text by the sign of engine values (e.g. cash answers say No when the forecast is overdrawn).

intents.missing_text: I need your preliminary tax answers first: how you work it out, and last year’s tax and what you paid for it. Add them in Farm data.
intents.text: About {result.due_on_pay_date} is due this autumn (31 October, or the ROS date in mid-November): {result.preliminary.amount} of preliminary tax for this year and {result.preceding_year.balance_due} left of last year’s. The lowest preliminary tax that avoids interest would be {result.lowest_safe.amount}. It’s an estimate: confirm it with your accountant.
follow_ups: Will I have cash for the December feed bill?
Why is my cash different from my profit?

intents.missing_text: I need a full year of figures to compare your profit with your cash.
intents.text: This year your accounts show a profit of {result.accounts_operating_profit}; the months should show {result.expected_operating_cash} of farm cash and they show {result.actual_operating_cash}. The gap is things that aren’t cash or are paid later: herd value {result.bridge.herd_value_change}, stock value {result.bridge.stock_value_change}, milk paid a month late {result.bridge.milk_debtors} and merchant credit {result.bridge.merchant_credit}. Not explained: {result.unexplained}.

intents.missing_text: Add your herd groups (head and value a head) under Year end in Farm data and I can value it.
intents.text: At market value your herd at 31 December is worth {result.total.market_value}. On Revenue practice, the value used for your profit and tax, it’s {result.total.revenue_practice_value}. A bank looks at the market value.
follow_ups: How much tax is due this autumn?
How much more could I borrow?

intents.text: Based on this year (actual + forecast), after {result.drawings} of drawings and {result.tax} of tax you can repay {result.repayment_capacity} a year, and your current loans take {result.debt_service}. A lender wanting {result.min_cover|times} cover could lend you up to {result.new_loan.max_principal} more over {result.new_loan.term_months|months}, at about {result.new_loan.monthly_payment_at_max} a month.
follow_ups: How much do I owe on my loans?

variants.text: Not at the moment. After {result.drawings} of drawings and {result.tax} of tax you can repay {result.repayment_capacity} a year, but your current loans take {result.debt_service} (cover after drawings and tax {result.repayment_cover|times}; a lender wants {result.min_cover|times}). Bringing that cover up comes before any new loan.

intents.text: Yes. You're projected to have {result.months[10].closing_cash} at the end of November and {result.closing_cash} on 31 December, after loan repayments.
follow_ups: How much do I owe on my loans?

variants.text: Not without going overdrawn. You're projected at {result.months[10].closing_cash} at the end of November and {result.closing_cash} on 31 December, after loan repayments. Agree overdraft cover with your bank or advisor before then.

intents.text: From January to September you made an Operating Surplus of {result.ytd.profit.net} on income of {result.ytd.revenue.total}, a {result.ytd.profit.margin_pct|pct} margin. Operating costs were {result.ytd.costs.total}. Loan repayments ({result.ytd.finance.loan_repayments}) are kept outside that surplus.
follow_ups: Will I have cash for the December feed bill?
How much do I owe on my loans?

intents.text: You owe {result.total_balance} across your loans and repay {result.total_monthly_payment} a month in total. The machinery loan is {result.loans[1].repaid_pct|pct} repaid; total interest still to pay is {result.total_interest}.
follow_ups: How much more could I borrow?
Will I have cash for the December feed bill?
